name: Graph Coarsening and Quotient Construction
problem_statement: Map every vertex to a nonempty coarse cluster and construct the weighted quotient graph with declared edge and feature aggregation.

normalization: Preserve external vertex identities and isolated vertices.
Reject self-loops and collapse parallel edges only under the declared aggregation rule.

problem_inputs.name: cluster_assignment
problem_inputs.description: Optional fixed assignment; null requests a declared clustering method.

problem_inputs.name: method
problem_inputs.description: Clustering method when an assignment is not supplied.

problem_inputs.name: self_loop_policy
problem_inputs.description: Whether intra-cluster edges survive as quotient self-loops.

problem_inputs.name: seed
problem_inputs.description: Random seed for a randomized clustering method.

required_outputs.name: fine_to_coarse
required_outputs.description: Total surjective mapping to the coarse vertex IDs.

required_outputs.name: coarse_graph
required_outputs.description: Quotient graph; parallel fine edges aggregate by sum.

required_outputs.name: cluster_sizes
required_outputs.description: Number of original vertices in each cluster.

solution_semantics.objective: Map every vertex to a nonempty coarse cluster and construct the weighted quotient graph with declared edge and feature aggregation.
solution_semantics.exactness: Clustering may be heuristic; quotient aggregation must be exact within numeric tolerance.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each external vertex ID occurs once; output multiplicities follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No ordering among equally valid solutions is required.

validation_rules: Every fine vertex occurs in exactly one nonempty cluster, including isolated vertices.
For each coarse edge, recompute the sum of corresponding original edge weights.
Undirected input edges are counted once, even if a GPU adapter stores symmetric arcs.
Recompute cluster sizes and requested feature reductions from the assignment.
edge_cases: A one-cluster quotient can contain a self-loop.
Greedy matching may leave singleton clusters.

correctness: Every fine vertex occurs in exactly one nonempty cluster, including isolated vertices.
